devdoc.details: NOVEL features vs MedRec (Azaria et al., 2016):   1. Auto-expiry consent — permissions revoke automatically at block.timestamp      No patient action needed — the contract enforces expiry automatically   2. Emergency override with penalty mechanism      Every access is permanently logged. Unjustified access = strike.      Three strikes = automatic suspension from the network.Cross-contract interaction:   This contract calls PatientRegistry to verify roles before   granting or revoking consent and before allowing emergency access.

PatientAlerted(address,address,uint256,u.details: NOVEL — patient is immediately alerted on-chain when emergency access occurs

ProviderPenalised(address,uint256,bool,u.details: NOVEL — emitted when emergency personnel receive a penalty strike

params._registryAddress: Address of the deployed PatientRegistry contract

emergencyAccess(address,string).details: Calls PatientRegistry to verify caller is registered emergency personnel      and that the patient is registered. Issues a 4-hour read-only token.      Patient is immediately alerted on-chain via PatientAlerted event.      Every access is permanently logged — records can never be deleted.

params._patient: Patient wallet address whose records are being accessed

grantConsent(address,uint256).details: Calls PatientRegistry to verify caller is a registered patient      and that the provider is a registered doctor/pharmacist/insurer.      Consent auto-expires at block.timestamp >= expiryTime — no patient action needed.

params._provider: Provider wallet address to grant access to

hasValidConsent(address,address).details: Called by HealthRecords before returning patient data      NOVEL — checks both active flag AND timestamp expiry

returns._0: true if consent is active and not yet expired

reviewAccess(uint256,bool,string).details: If unjustified, _penalisePersonnel is called automatically.      Three unjustified accesses = automatic suspension.

params._eventId: The emergency event ID to review
params._isJustified: Whether the access was clinically justified

revokeConsent(address).details: Calls PatientRegistry to verify caller is a registered patient

params._provider: Provider wallet address to revoke access from

consents.details: NOVEL — auto-expiry checked at call time, no cron job needed

constructor.notice: Sets admin and links to the deployed PatientRegistry contract

credentials(address).notice: Penalty record for each emergency personnel address

emergencyAccess(address,string).notice: NOVEL — Emergency personnel access records without prior consent

emergencyEvents(uint256).notice: Permanent registry of all emergency events — immutable audit trail

getConsentExpiry(address,address).notice: Returns the expiry timestamp for a provider's consent (0 if none)

getCredential(address).notice: Returns penalty info for emergency personnel

getEmergencyLogCount().notice: Returns total number of emergency events ever logged

grantConsent(address,uint256).notice: NOVEL — Grant time-limited consent to a provider

hasValidConsent(address,address).notice: Check if a provider currently has valid non-expired consent

patientEmergencyLog(address,uint256).notice: patient => list of emergency event IDs affecting them

registry().notice: Reference to PatientRegistry for cross-contract role verification

reviewAccess(uint256,bool,string).notice: NOVEL — Governance review of an emergency access event

revokeConsent(address).notice: Manually revoke a provider's consent before expiry

totalEmergencyEvents().notice: Total number of emergency events ever logged

userdoc.notice: Contract 2 of 3 — Consent and Emergency Access Management         Manages time-limited consent grants between patients and providers.         Handles emergency override with permanent on-chain logging.         Called by HealthRecords before returning any patient data.

devdoc.author: Ananya Aastha — N12125547 | IFB452 Blockchain Technology, QUT
devdoc.details: Cross-contract interactions:   This contract calls PatientRegistry to verify stakeholder roles.   This contract calls AccessControl to verify consent before returning data.   This demonstrates direct smart contract interaction as required by the spec.Architecture:   PatientRegistry  ←── HealthRecords ──→  AccessControl        ↑                                        ↑   role checks                          consent checks

addRecord(address,string,bytes32,uint8).details: Calls PatientRegistry to verify patient is registered.      Calls AccessControl to verify consent for doctors and pharmacists.      Only the IPFS hash is stored — raw data lives off-chain on IPFS.

params._fileHash: keccak256 hash of the file for integrity verification
params._ipfsHash: IPFS CID of the encrypted medical file
params._recordType: Type of medical record being added

params._accessControlAddress: Address of the deployed AccessControl contract
params._registryAddress: Address of the deployed PatientRegistry contract

returns._0: Number of records stored for this patient

getRecords(address).details: Calls PatientRegistry to verify roles.      Calls AccessControl to verify consent for doctors/pharmacists/insurers.      Emergency personnel can access without consent — audit log in AccessControl.

params._patient: Patient wallet address whose records to retrieve

returns._0: Array of Record structs belonging to the patient

userdoc.notice: Contract 3 of 3 — Health Record Storage and Retrieval         Stores IPFS hashes of encrypted medical records on-chain.         Raw medical data is stored off-chain on IPFS — only the CID         and a keccak256 integrity hash are stored on-chain.

devdoc.author: Ananya Aastha — N12125547 | IFB452 Blockchain Technology, QUT
devdoc.details: Stakeholders:   1. Patient          — self-registers using their wallet   2. Doctor           — registered by admin after credential verification   3. Pharmacist       — registered by admin   4. Insurer          — registered by admin, read-only with patient consent   5. Emergency        — registered by admin, bypass consent in emergencies   6. Regulator        — registered by admin, anonymised audit access only

params._doctor: Wallet address of the doctor to register

registerEmergencyPersonnel(address).details: Emergency personnel can bypass consent in genuine emergencies

params._person: Wallet address of the emergency personnel to register

params._insurer: Wallet address of the insurer to register

registerPatient().details: No admin approval needed — patients own their registration

params._pharmacist: Wallet address of the pharmacist to register

params._regulator: Wallet address of the regulator to register

@title PatientRegistry
 @author Ananya Aastha — N12125547 | IFB452 Blockchain Technology, QUT
 @notice Contract 1 of 3 — Stakeholder Registration
         Manages all role assignments for the DHRSS system.
         This is the source of truth for identity verification.
         AccessControl and HealthRecords call this contract to verify roles
         before performing any sensitive operations.
 @dev Stakeholders:
   1. Patient          — self-registers using their wallet
   2. Doctor           — registered by admin after credential verification
   3. Pharmacist       — registered by admin
   4. Insurer          — registered by admin, read-only with patient consent
   5. Emergency        — registered by admin, bypass consent in emergencies
   6. Regulator        — registered by admin, anonymised audit access only
@notice Address of the contract deployer — has admin privileges
@notice Role registries — one mapping per stakeholder type
@notice Emitted when a patient self-registers
@notice Emitted when admin registers any provider role
@dev Restricts function to the contract deployer only

 @dev No admin approval needed — patients own their registration
